scope: Legacy mutable state and side effects inventoried for migration across the declared application, deployed-worker and operational-script production roots, including each distinct lexical scope containing an AST-visible writer use before the research-kernel cutover.

excluded_python_roots.migrations: Alembic revision history is schema/deployment authority, including historical DML and backfills. Revisions are immutable and reviewed separately through the migration chain; they are not runtime scientific-state write-owner surfaces.
excluded_python_roots.tests: Test-only fixtures and temporary writes are outside deployed application, worker and operator-script authority.

policy.legacy_source_ast_review_limit: This normalized-AST backstop freezes every parseable Python file in the declared legacy production roots after explicitly removing new-authority and migration-tooling roots. It catches added, removed or semantically changed legacy Python source even when a specialized sink scanner does not recognize the syntax; comments, formatting, generated runtime code, non-Python launchers and the explicitly excluded roots are outside this digest.
policy.migration_source_ast_review_limit: Migration tooling and immutable Alembic revision history have a separate normalized-AST freeze. Historical schema DML/backfills remain deployment authority reviewed through the migration chain rather than runtime scientific write owners.
policy.non_python_invocation_source_review_limi: Every Git-indexed frontend source/configuration file, recursive shell launcher, non-Python docker launcher and root docker-compose YAML is frozen by exact relative path, regular-file Git mode and byte SHA. Symlinks and non-regular Git modes fail closed. Generated frontend/.next, frontend/node_modules and docker Python already covered by the production AST graph are excluded. The byte freeze catches otherwise-unrecognized syntax but does not infer runtime behavior of generated or third-party code.
policy.scientific_cutover: Freeze and content-address the legacy source, issue an import receipt, commit through exactly one target owner, then make the legacy surface read-only.
policy.service_boundary_limit: This mechanically freezes statically declared aletheia.memory.service imports and imported-name uses across aletheia and operational scripts in module and nested lexical scopes. It does not claim to discover arbitrary dynamic imports or direct ORM, SQL, filesystem or external-system mutations; those are handled by separate reviewed surface baselines.
policy.allowed_legacy_caller_scope: Every current aletheia-package caller must be covered by allowed_legacy_callers. Operational scripts are fully frozen in call_sites and may be omitted from the post-cutover application allowlist.

aletheia.observations.store._append_exac.dispatch_rule: Each listed public writer must pass one literal SQLAlchemy record type through the record_type keyword; the shared helper cannot select a table independently.

writer_surface_static_resolution_excepti.execution.transactional_outbox: PR-4b composes the immutable runtime-v2 terminal intent writers and PR-8e adds a column-restricted v1 publication/spool service, while the uncalled v1 compatibility source writer remains; exact callers and direct ORM mutation scopes are frozen separately.
writer_surface_static_resolution_excepti.research_store.transactional_outbox: The authority-minimal PostgreSQLResearchKernelOutbox caller-owned publication surface is composed by the controller dispatcher; the full-store transaction-owning mark_outbox_published wrapper remains an explicit uncalled compatibility surface.

policy.direct_file_sink_review_limit: The baseline covers direct Path/open/os.write, archive-open modes, atomic replace, serializer, dataframe and plotting file sinks across the declared aletheia, deployed docker-worker and recursive operational-script roots. Indirect library-internal writes, arbitrary dynamic dispatch and external systems remain separate reviewed boundaries.
policy.direct_external_sink_review_limit: The baseline covers AST-visible EventBus-style publish calls, outbound HTTP mutation calls, known model-provider and GitHub mutation methods, and subprocess launch calls across the declared aletheia, deployed docker-worker and recursive operational-script roots. It does not claim to discover dynamically dispatched SDK methods, hidden library network I/O, non-Python launchers, or runtime monkeypatching.
policy.direct_orm_authority_source: Every resolved table is classified by the postgres storage_target/storage_targets records in this inventory; non-constructor mutation scopes must match a declared legacy_entrypoint or additional_writers symbol.
policy.direct_orm_review_limit: This static AST baseline resolves explicit imports/re-exports and aliases for every declared SQLAlchemy model; ORM class self/cls bindings; model construction; query/get/select/scalar result flows; attribute, setattr and relationship mutation; explicit aliases of recognized setattr/session/query/table/SQLAlchemy mutation callables; session add/delete/merge/bulk APIs; SQLAlchemy/table/query insert/update/delete; literal mutating SQL; and fail-closed f-string/binary SQL edges. The sole declared dynamic SQL scope is the SHA-pinned qualification role/database/ACL DDL transaction below; it is operational host commissioning rather than an ORM-table writer. It does not claim to resolve dynamic imports, reflection-generated models, runtime monkeypatching, helper-returned model instances, dynamically selected mutator callables, or other dynamic SQL hidden behind an untyped variable; any semantic change in legacy Python remains guarded by the separate normalized-AST source freeze.

direct_dynamic_sql_writers.mutation_scope: three exact roles, database owner, former-admin database grant removal, and rendered qualification ACL in one transaction

policy.protected_orm_reference_limit: Every explicit import and AST-visible reference to the Claim, ClaimEvidence and BeliefState ORM types in deployed Python roots is frozen. Dynamic imports, reflection and string-based model lookup remain outside this static gate.
